full_judgment:
Md. Awlad Ali, J: This Rule arises out of the impugned Re-notice for auction sale dated 19.09.2004 published in the daily "Janakantha" (Annexure-M) at the instance of the respondent No. 4 the Chief Regional Manager, Regional Office, Bangladesh Krishi Bank. Plot No. 3, Block No. A. Mirpur-13, Dhaka for sale of the property under Khatian No. 10/5 comprising plot No. 900, land measuring 0.0875 acres of Mouja Jurain under P.S. Demra/Shampur, Dhaka and land measuring o.0438/0. 1313 under khatian No. 10/3 comprising plot No. 900 of the said Mouja. 

 2. The facts relevant for the disposal of the Rule briefly are that, the petitioner is the owner of the properties as mentioned in the auction sale notice. The petitioner on 13.08.1987 executed a power of attorney in favour of her husband who was the promoter of M/S Delwara Oil Mills. On 23.12.1989 the promoter of the said Oil Mills the husband of the petitioner had died and as a result the project of the said Mills was not implemented. The petitioner on 18.05.1991 made an application to the respondent bank stating inter-alia that the said Oil Mills has not been installed and the imported machineries were lying in packed condition. The petitioner also requested the Bank to waive the interest on the loan granted. Subsequently the petitioner made another application to the respondent bank to sell the imported machineries of the proposed mill and adjust the loan money with the sale proceeds of the machineries. The petitioner also stated in that application that after adjustment the rest amount will be paid by installment. The respondent bank in their meeting held on 24.04.1994 and 25.04.1994 took a decision to sell the imported machineries and adjust the loan money which is also evident from the resolution dated 07.05.1994. The respondent bank decided that after adjustment of the loan money in the manner aforesaid Branch Manager will take initiative to "write off' the loan amount. The petitioner on 14.06.2003 made an application to the respondent bank to implement the resolution adopted in the meeting dated 7.5.94 (Annexure-E). On 09.08.2003 the respondent bank issued a letter to the petitioner stating that the loan money cannot be written off, but 50% interest on the loan may be waived and the respondent bank asked the petitioner to contact with the Jurain Branch within 7 (seven) days for taking necessary step to pay the loan amount. Thereafter, on 02.09.2003 the respondent No. 5, Manager, Bangladesh Krishi bank, Jurain Branch issued a notice to the petitioner demanding Tk. 65,21,198.60/. (Annexure-H). Then on 22.09.2003 the respondent No. 5 issued another notice demanding of the petitioner to pay the aforesaid amount within one month. Having received the notice dated 22.09.2003 the petitioner filed Title Suit No. 316/2003 in the 4th Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka for a declaration that the notice dated 22.09.2003 is void and not binding upon the petitioner. The petitioner also filed and application for temporary injunction whereupon the learned Court vide order dated 26.10.2003 issued a show cause notice as to why the order of injunction should not be granted. On 29.10.2003 the respondent bank published a sale notice in the daily Prothom  Alo to sell the said properties (Annexure-K). On 11.11.2003 the learned Joint District Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka after hearing bolt the parties was pleased to pass an ad-interim in-junction in favour of the petitioner restraining the respondents to sell the properties. The interim injunction order was vacated on 02.08.2004 and thereafter on 19.09.2004 the respondent bank published the impugned Re-notice for auction sale of the property in the Daily Janakantha. The petitioner on 25.9.2004 served a Demand of Justice Notice upon the respondents requesting them to cancel the impugned notice. It is contended that the respondent Bank is not authorized to sell the property without filing any suit and the impugned sale notice is liable to be declared to have been issued without any lawful authority. 

 3. The respondent No. 5 Manager, Krishi Bank, Jurain Branch, Dhaka has filed affidavit-in-opposition and also filed a supplementary affidavit stating inter alia, that the petitioner prayed for sanctioning loan for importing machineries for establishment of M/S. Delwara Oil Mills. The respondent Bank sanctioned an amount of Tk. 18,23,000/- in favour of the petitioner’s husband the promoter of the said Mills for importing machineries through a letter of credit but the petitioner neither established the said M/S Delware Oil Mills nor did the petitioner repay the loan amount in time. The loan was sanctioned in favour of the petitioner by sanction letter dated 25.11.87 and the petitioner signed a deed of agreement on the said date and also executed and registered a. mortgage deed in respect of the property mentioned in the schedule of the notice. The petitioner's husband opened the letter of credit being L.C. No. BKB/L.C/ADB-657/88/176 dated 03.02. 1988 and the petitioner imported the machineries under the said L.C. worth Tk. 17.38.576.78, but the promoter could not establish the said Mills, and the promoter died on 23.12.1989 after one year and ten months of the importation of the machineries. It is contended that under section 12(1)(2) and (3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the bank has exclusive power to auction sell the mortgaged property and accordingly the respondent bank issued the impugned notice for sale of the property without the intervention of the Court. The mortgaged deed was executed by the petitioner on 29.12.1987 being deed No. 46 of 1987-88 (Annexure-1).
